project.name: audioldm2
project.description: AudioLDM 2 is a Python toolkit for text-to-audio and text-to-music generation, text-to-speech generation, and super-resolution inpainting.

nodes.name: MANIFEST.in
nodes.summary: Declares the Python source distribution assets, including top-level metadata and AudioLDM2 text, Python, compressed, NumPy, and JSON resources.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Introduces AudioLDM 2 and documents installation, web and command-line use, seed behavior, pretrained models, Diffusers integration, and citation information across 12 sections.

nodes.name: app.py

nodes.name: text2audio

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to learn what AudioLDM 2 generates, which pretrained variants it exposes, and how its text-to-audio, music, speech, and inpainting workflows are invoked. It supplies the user-facing vocabulary for the model path that the rest of this tour follows.

tour.title: Inference Entry Points
tour.description: The Gradio application and package CLI are the two executable fronts to the system: one lazily serves selectable checkpoints and playable candidates, while the other dispatches generation and restoration modes. Read them together to see how user arguments become calls into the shared Python pipeline.
tour.languageLesson: Python's __main__.py gives a package an executable surface through `python -m package`, while keeping the reusable implementation in importable modules.

tour.title: Pipeline and Checkpoints
tour.description: Building on the entry points, the public pipeline batches prompts, selects generation or super-resolution/inpainting behavior, and loads the requested checkpoint. The runtime helpers supply deterministic seeding, Hugging Face downloads, dynamic construction, waveform output, and the complete model configuration that binds the checkpoint to its component classes.

tour.title: Multimodal Conditioning
tour.description: The conditioning module turns each prompt batch into the representations consumed by diffusion, combining Flan-T5 language features, phoneme sequences, AudioMAE features, and CLAP embeddings with matching unconditional paths for classifier-free guidance. The phoneme encoder and AudioMAE wrapper show how linguistic detail and spectrogram context enter that shared conditioning contract.

tour.title: CLAP Configuration
tour.description: CLAP contributes aligned audio-text semantics used to condition generation and assess candidate relevance. Its model code builds the encoders and projection heads, while the JSON record makes one concrete HTS-AT choice explicit: a 48 kHz audio frontend, 768-dimensional embedding, and 12-layer text transformer; this conditioning sample rate is distinct from the final 16 kHz waveform codec path.
tour.languageLesson: JSON configuration keeps architecture dimensions and frontend parameters data-driven, allowing the factory code to construct model variants without duplicating Python implementations.

tour.title: AudioMAE Token Bridge
tour.description: After the raw conditioning streams are formed, a GPT-2-based autoregressive bridge projects and combines them into predicted AudioMAE token embeddings. These generated semantic tokens provide the sequence-level context handed to the latent diffusion model, connecting the text and audio encoders from the previous steps to denoising.

tour.title: Latent Diffusion Core
tour.description: The DDPM module owns the conditioned latent-generation pipeline and wraps the denoising network, making it the central coordinator after conditioning is complete. The OpenAI-style UNet supplies timestep-aware residual and attention blocks that predict how noisy audio latents should be updated at each sampling step.

tour.title: DDIM Sampling Loop
tour.description: DDIM turns the diffusion model into the practical inference loop by building the schedule, applying classifier-free guidance, and iteratively denoising latent candidates. This is where the conditional and unconditional representations from Step 4 are combined to trade prompt adherence against diversity before the latent is decoded.

tour.title: Mel Latent Codec
tour.description: The first-stage codec is a KL-regularized autoencoder over mel spectrograms: during generation it maps the denoised latent back into the mel domain and then delegates waveform synthesis to its configured vocoder. Its convolutional encoder/decoder blocks and Gaussian latent distribution explain the representation boundary between diffusion space and audible output.

tour.title: HiFi-GAN Waveform Decode
tour.description: HiFi-GAN is the audio decoder that converts the reconstructed mel features from Step 9 into waveform samples through residual convolutional upsampling blocks. The model utility constructs the vocoder, reconciles checkpoint keys, clips the result, and emits the final 16-bit, 16 kHz audio representation used by the public pipeline.

tour.title: Runtime Environment
tour.description: Finish with the dependency record that establishes the PyTorch, Hugging Face Hub, and pinned Transformers environment used by the example inference scripts. It connects the architectural tour back to a reproducible runtime in which checkpoint download, conditioning, diffusion, codec decode, and waveform output can execute end to end.
